§1 — A model, not a fit

The evidence is in jt60sa-booster-ripple-evidence. The claim this sprint has to support is that we can model a tokamak power supply well enough to predict the effect of a design change before it is built. That is only possible if the model is built from the circuit, not learned from the waveform. The difference decides what each piece is allowed to be:

PieceWhere it comes fromFitted?
Topology: six-pulse bridges, transformers, series inductance, coil, filter network, groundingDesign documents and literatureNo
Firing law: the bridge firing angle that produces the commanded mean voltageThyristor-bridge physics (mean output proportional to the cosine of the firing angle, less the commutation drop)No; the reference is measured
Supply frequency, its sag through a pulseMeasured directly from the ripple linesNo
Line voltage per bridge, commutation reactanceTwo physical quantities with nameplate values to check againstYes, on 2021 data
Series inductance and resistance, coil self- and mutual inductancesCircuit quantities with design values to check againstYes, on 2021 data
Measurement chain: bandwidth and digitiser interleave mismatchInstrument quantitiesYes, on 2021 data
Filter components, grounding resistorsDesign valuesNever

That leaves about eight fitted numbers against thousands of harmonic constraints per shot. Each fitted number is a physical quantity whose value can be checked against a nameplate. A black-box fit, such as a transfer function or a network trained on the 2021 waveforms, would reproduce 2021 and could say nothing about adding a 0.75 mF capacitor. This model can, because the capacitor enters as a component, not as a coefficient. The prediction test itself is filter-grounding-prediction. No circuit simulator such as SPICE or PSCAD is needed. The controller sets the firing instants, not the circuit state, so the bridge output can be written in closed form, with commutation overlap handled analytically. Everything downstream is a linear network. A switching-level simulator earns its place only for commutation failures, snubbers or interaction with the motor-generator, none of which this question needs.

§2 — The bridge as a switching function

Add src/power_convertor/bridge.py. It gives the output voltage of a six-pulse thyristor bridge fed from a three-phase source at a given firing angle and commutation overlap, sampled on any time base. Overlap follows from the commutation reactance and the load current. A pair of bridges with a configurable phase shift between their transformers gives twelve-pulse operation. The source frequency may vary slowly in time, because the motor-generator sags through a pulse. Also provide the harmonic phasors of one supply cycle, for the frequency-domain path.

Done when tests/test_bridge.py passes four checks:

  • The harmonic amplitudes of an ideal bridge (zero overlap) match the textbook expression at three firing angles, to 1%.
  • The mean output equals the line voltage times 1.35 times the cosine of the firing angle, less the commutation drop.
  • A pair at 30° cancels the 6f, 18f and 30f lines to below 1% of a single bridge's.
  • Negative control: a pair at 0° does not cancel them.

§3 — The measurement chain

Model the coil-voltage channel as a band-limited, two-way time-interleaved digitiser sampling at 4 kHz. It has a bandwidth parameter and a gain mismatch between the interleaved channels. Every model output is passed through it before comparison, aliasing included, so model and measurement are compared in the same domain.

The measured side already exists and is reused, not rebuilt: power_convertor.signals (ripple, spectrum, line_amplitudes) and power_convertor.fold (supply_frequency, fold). This section lifts the idle-window measurement out of scripts/figures/jt60sa_booster_ripple.py (measure(), IDLE, ORDERS) into the library, adds the peak-to-peak of the folded ripple to what it returns, and has the figure script import it, so the model and the measurement share one definition of a line and of the peak-to-peak ripple.

Done when the chain, applied to the §2 bridge output with the fitted parameters, reproduces the image lines at 2000 − k × 367 Hz (k = 1–4) in E100310's idle window to within 30% in amplitude. A fit with the gain mismatch fixed at zero, the negative control, fails to produce them. The parameters and residuals are recorded in this plan's evidence fragment.

§4 — The circuit: series inductance and coil coupling

Identify the loop the booster drives: the series inductance and resistance between converter and coil, the coil's self-inductance and its mutual inductances to the neighbouring coils. Use two independent routes:

  • The slow voltage–current balance, V = L dI/dt + Σ M dI_j/dt + R I, over the 2021 swing tests, with all ten coil currents measured.
  • The ripple pickup ratios on EF4, EF6 and EF1 during the EF5 tests. A pickup ratio is the mutual-to-self ratio M/L directly, so this route gives the coupling ratios, not the self-inductance.

Done when the voltage–current balance gives EF5's self-inductance within 20% of the design value from the JT-60SA magnet papers, with the value and citation recorded. The mutual-to-self ratios it implies for EF4, EF6 and EF1 agree with the pickup ratios within 20%; that is the cross-check between the two routes. As a negative control, the balance fitted with the coupling to EF4 and EF6 removed leaves a residual at least twice as large.

The identification lives in its own module, src/power_convertor/circuit.py. The loop the identified values load into is owned by power_convertor.filter_network, which filter-grounding-prediction §2 extends with the coil inductances as inputs; this section builds no second loop.

§5 — Fit on 2021, check on held-out 2021 shots

Fit the bridge line voltage, the commutation reactance and the series inductance on the EF5 ±1 kV idle window (E100310), with the measurement chain from §3 (its timing skew and gain mismatch; its fitted bandwidth is not carried over) and the circuit from §4. The coil self-inductance is the geometry value, 0.3749 H. Fast-discharge measurements on CS1–4, EF1, EF3 and EF4 fall 1–8% below or near their geometry values (CS1 −7.9% at worst; 7 of 13 within 3%), and the swing-balance 0.258 H is reported as a sensitivity until §6 explains it. The window carries base-supply ripple as well as the booster's: EF5's base supply put 119 V on 12f in 2021 with no booster current (E100303), a quarter to two-fifths of the 12f line in the fit window (jt60sa-booster-ripple-evidence §9). The model therefore carries the base supply as a second source, a twelve-pulse configuration of the §2 bridge pair, so the fit does not assign base ripple to the booster. Base lines change with the operating point (24f on EF2 and EF5 is 30–55 V at −2.3 to −4.2 kA and under 10 V near zero current), so the base source is not a fixed amplitude. It runs at each window's own base reference (PSSCfst/refvol<coil>Bse) and measured coil current. Its line voltage and commutation reactance are fitted first, on EF3 and EF4: they have no booster and belong to the same twelve-pulse family, and the fit spans the currents those coils saw in 2021. The values are then held fixed in the booster fit. E100303, EF5's own base at zero booster current, is the check on that transfer. Then predict, without refitting, three held-out cases:

  • The EF5 ±3 kV and ±5 kV tests (E100307, E100318), which have different firing angles.
  • The EF2 idle window (E100321), on the hypothesis that the boosters share a design. EF6 (E100347) is reported, not judged: its base supply is the other family (6f and 18f, the even lines nearly absent), whose arrangement jt60sa-power-supply-sources §7 has not yet cited, so a miss there could not be attributed to the booster.
  • The swing periods of each, at a different coil current.

The acceptance criteria are the ones pre-registered in filter-grounding-prediction §1. Fitting does not start until they are recorded there.

Done when every held-out case meets the pre-registered criteria for the 6f–24f lines and for the peak-to-peak ripple. A case that fails keeps this section open: its residuals are recorded in a comment, and the model is revised in a new section. Amended 2026-10-13: filter-grounding-prediction §4 was gated on this verdict until the lead decided, on 2026-10-13, to predict 2023 with the model as it stands. Gate g-fgp-2 is passed, and its evidence records this section's failing line check. The fitted line voltage and commutation reactance are compared with the JT-60U transformer ratings found in jt60sa-power-supply-sources. A control model with the pair fired symmetrically (balanced twelve-pulse), fitted to the same 2021 window, fails the criteria. That rejects symmetric firing, not the hardware: the documented booster is a 30° series pair, and asymmetric firing defeats its cancellation (jt60sa-power-supply-sources §2). This section's fit uses a single six-pulse bridge as the equivalent of that pair under asymmetric firing, and a series pair at one firing angle as the equivalent of the base supply. §8 replaces the base equivalent and §9 the booster equivalent with the documented structures. Figures go in docs/figures/booster-converter-model/.

§6 — Why the swing balance reads EF5's self-inductance 31% low

§4's swing balance gives EF5 0.258 H, stable across three shots and two estimators. The geometry value is 0.3749 H. Fast-discharge measurements, coil voltage against its own dI/dt over 3 s (scripts/jt60sa/fast_discharge_couplings.py, data/jt60sa/fast_discharge_couplings.json), fall within 1–8% of geometry on CS1–4, EF1, EF3 and EF4 (CS1 −7.9% at worst), and the 11 booster-swing coupling pairs sit at a median 0.989 of nova's M/L (jt60sa-coil-circuit-model, measured coupling matrix). That points to a defect in the swing balance, not to a wrong geometry. Candidates to test against the data: the window and its slow-part filter; an offset or scale in MMSYS/volEF5 during booster operation; the resistive term absorbing inductive voltage; eddy currents in passive structures over the swing's time scale. EF5's only 2021 dump (E100276) failed like the other February dumps, so another dump of EF5 is the direct check if one exists in the fast-discharge catalogue.

Done when the fragment names the mechanism, confirmed on a second shot or on a sibling coil run through the same identify_split. Positive control: EF3 or EF4 through the swing balance returns its dump value within 10%. Or the section records that the swing balance agrees with the dumps on sibling coils and fails only on EF5, with the EF5-specific test that would decide it.

§7 — One supply frequency or two: the lock behind every line and the fold

measurement.measure locks one supply frequency on the 12f line and uses it for every line and for the fold. On EF6 E100347 that lock gives 61.1672 Hz against 61.1299 Hz from the 6f line (commit 8edce2a), and the folded peak-to-peak moves from 2034 V to 3122 V while the 6f line stays at 1434 V. Over the 2.5 s window, 0.04 Hz drifts the 6f component by about 200°, which smears the fold, and costs the line estimate up to about 2.5 dB. That is most of the pre-registered 3 dB band. One explanation is that the base supplies and the boosters run from sources at slightly different frequencies: the base supplies own 12f and 24f on EF2–EF5, and the boosters own 6f and 18f there.

Measure each line's own frequency with fold.fit_line per order, per coil and per shot, across the 2021 and 2023 idle windows and a booster-free shot (E101088). Establish whether the 6f and 12f families sit at distinct frequencies, and by how much. Then make measure estimate each line at its own frequency. Fold each source family at its own frequency, and define the folded peak-to-peak for a two-frequency window as the peak-to-peak of the sum of the per-family folds. The measured and modelled sides use the same definition.

Done when the fragment tabulates the per-line frequencies for EF5, EF2, EF6, EF3 and EF4 in the named windows and states whether the families differ beyond the fit's uncertainty. tests/test_measurement.py shows a synthetic two-frequency signal measured to within 1% per line and per family fold. Negative control: the single 12f lock must miss a 6f line offset by 0.04 Hz by more than 1 dB. E100347 is re-measured under the new definition. The change to filter-grounding-prediction §1's measurement column is recorded there as an amendment made before any 2023 prediction was computed.

§8 — The base supply as documented: parallel modules and their operating modes

§5 carries the base supply as a series pair at one firing angle. The sources plan has since cited the hardware. The CEA base supply of EF2–EF5 is four parallel modules at +15°, −15°, 0° and −30°, each bridge with its own reactor (Novello 2015; Plant Integration Document, pp. 139–141). Novello p. 1123 sets the operating-mode rule. Circulating mode begins when the coil current falls below 1 kA; the internal circulating current is then held constant, and its ripple is limited to 500 A. Above 1 kA the modules conduct in one current direction. Whether 24f cancels depends on which modules conduct. In the signed circulating mode the groups cancel 24f; with all groups conducting in one direction the same phases leave about 81 V at 24f at the register's nominal 715 V line voltage (jt60sa-power-supply-sources §7 register). The circulating mode at low coil current is the documented candidate for the E100303 miss: 52.05 V predicted at 24f against 1.90 V measured.

Model the base from its cited configuration in power_convertor.configurations (filter-grounding-prediction §3): parallel modules sharing the coil current through their reactors, with the mode chosen from the coil current by the documented 1 kA rule. Refit the base's line voltage and commutation reactance on EF3 and EF4 under this structure. Then hold them fixed for §9.

The first refit (merged at cd38228) read one-direction operation as all four modules conducting equally. That reading cancels 12f exactly, and the multi-kA EF3/EF4 windows refute it: 0 V predicted against 91–133 V measured, in all twelve windows at 1.1–5.0 kA. The one-direction mode is therefore carried as a stated hypothesis. In one-direction operation the 30°-apart pair for that current direction conducts, which is twelve-pulse and keeps 12f and 24f. The circulating mode at low coil current keeps the signed pairing that cancels 24f. The pairing is inferred, not cited; filter-grounding-prediction §3 already marks it as a hypothesis.

Done when the E100303 transfer, EF5's own base at zero booster current, meets the §1 bands on the lines the base produces (12f and 24f) and on the folded peak-to-peak, through the actual source-to-coil scoring path in supply.py. The 6f, 18f and 30f lines, which every base mode cancels, are reported as booster-family lines. The EF3/EF4 multi-kA refit under the pairing hypothesis meets the same bands on 12f and 24f. A line that fails keeps this section open, and the fragment records which line and why. §9 may proceed on the best available base. Its verdict reports the base-family lines (12f, 24f) separately from the booster-family lines (6f, 18f, 30f), and §9 cannot close while a base line it depends on fails here. The EF3/EF4 refit residuals are reported beside the §5 first-node values. Negative control: the same modules with every group forced to one current direction at low coil current must restore the 24f line, about 81 V at the register's nominal 715 V, and fail E100303's 24f. A wrong-phase control, with all module phases set to 0°, must fail the EF3/EF4 family signature.

§9 — The booster as documented: a 30° series pair under asymmetric firing

§5's six-pulse equivalent fails all six judged held-out cases. One bridge cannot reach the ±3 kV and ±5 kV swing references, its maximum mean output being about 2.6 kV, and its fitted voltage sits a third below the 2.9 kV nameplate. The documented booster is four converters in two series and antiparallel pairs whose transformers sit 30° apart, and asymmetric firing defeats the pair's cancellation (Shimada 2013, pp. 185–186). The booster has two transformer pairs: PSV21/22 at 2.9 kV and 2.9 kV, giving up to 2 × 3.92 ≈ 7.8 kV, and PSV11/12 at 3.16 kV and 2.1 kV, giving about 1.35 × (3.16 + 2.1) ≈ 7.1 kV. Which pair feeds which coil is open. The firing mode in operation is open.

Extend the bridge-pair library so each bridge of a pair takes its own firing angle, and pin the transformer phase orientation with an independent complex-phasor test: negating every phase must fail it. Model the booster from its cited configuration. The asymmetric firing law is a hypothesis: state it, and fit at most one parameter for it. Hold §8's best available base fixed, and report base-line and booster-line residuals separately. Fit on E100310, then re-score §5's held-out cases under the same pre-registered bands.

Done when every judged held-out case meets the §1 criteria under the documented pair. The pair must reach the ±3 kV and ±5 kV swing references, and the fitted secondary voltages must sit within 10% of one of the two documented pairs, 2.9/2.9 kV or 3.16/2.1 kV, with the pair named. A case that fails keeps this section, and §5, open: the fragment records its residuals beside §5's equivalent. Filter-grounding-prediction §4 no longer waits on this verdict: the lead decided on 2026-10-13 to predict 2023 with the model as it stands, and g-fgp-2's evidence records the failing line check. Negative control: the same pair fired symmetrically must cancel 6f, 18f and 30f and fail the 2021 lines.

§10 — Seed each line from the window's own fundamental, then re-score the base

measurement.measure seeds each line's frequency search at order × 61.2 Hz within ±3 Hz. The supply runs between 61.0 and 61.2 Hz, so at 24f a window near 61.0 Hz puts the line 4.8 Hz outside the search. The estimate then reads noise: 3.1 V against 41.6 V on E100340 EF4. Every line estimate since §7 carries this risk at high orders, and so do the judged criteria.

Seed every line from the window's own fitted fundamental, the 6f or 12f line, whichever dominates, then refine per line as §7 does.

Done when tests/test_measurement.py shows a synthetic window at 61.0 Hz measuring 24f and 30f within 1%, and the old fixed seed failing that test. The fragment re-scores §8's twelve EF3/EF4 windows on 24f and E100303 on 12f and 24f with the corrected measure, beside the §8 values. §5's six-pulse held-out verdicts are re-scored where a line moves by more than 0.5 dB, and every judged figure stated in §5, §7 and §8 that the correction changes is listed with its old and new value. Negative control: the fixed 61.2 Hz seed must miss the synthetic 61.0 Hz 24f line by more than 3 dB.

§11 — The ENEA two-module base in one-direction mode

§8's pairing for one-direction operation is written for the CEA four-module base. For the ENEA two-module base of CS1–4, EF1 and EF6 (phase groups 0/−30° or +15/−15°, two current directions), the code now raises where it used to return weights, so a one-direction ENEA operating point cannot be modelled. No caller builds one yet, but EF1/EF6 base modelling will.

Done when the one-direction mode returns the documented ENEA weights, the module carrying the current's direction, and tests/test_supply.py shows an ENEA base in one-direction mode keeping 6f and 18f, the family signature at zero current in jt60sa-power-supply-sources §7, and failing when the two modules are forced to the same phase.

§12 — One measurement owner for idle and swing windows

§9's fit script measures swing windows with its own copy of measurement.measure's frequency anchoring and family folding. The independent review scored reuse at 5 against a floor of 10, so swing and idle results can drift apart.

Done when measurement.measure handles swing windows, where the coil current and the supply frequency move, and scripts/figures/booster_converter_fit.py calls it for both idle and swing windows with no measurement logic of its own. tests/test_measurement.py shows a synthetic swing window measured within 1% per line, and the copied path deleted. Re-running §9's eight cases through measure() reproduces their recorded measured lines within 0.1 dB, or the fragment lists each line that moves with its old and new value. Negative control: a swing window measured with a single stationary frequency must miss a sagging line by more than 1 dB.

§13 — Why the frozen pair's 18f, 24f and 30f phases sit far from the recorded ones

The §9 overlay aligns the frozen model to the recorded idle samples with one supply phase. 6f and 12f then agree within 13°, while 18f, 24f and 30f sit 124°–172° away. The model's folded 36f and 42f lines are also 10 and 2.3 times the recorded ones. The fit matched only the 6f, 18f and 30f amplitudes on E100310, so the line phases and the high orders are unconstrained. Since its 2026-10-13 amendment, filter-grounding-prediction §1 judges phase within 30°.

Test candidate explanations on 2021 data only. No 2023 shot is read. The candidates:

  • Commutation overlap. A larger commutation reactance lengthens the overlap, which suppresses the high orders and turns the phases of the higher lines. The amplitude-only fit may have traded reactance against firing offset.
  • The analogue bandwidth that §3 fitted and §5 does not carry. A one-pole lag is bounded at 90°, so it cannot alone explain errors past 120°, though it would attenuate the high orders.
  • Which bridge of the pair leads, and the firing law's phase structure (§9's firing-law diagnosis).
  • The base's contribution at 12f and 24f on these booster coils.

Done when each candidate is confirmed or ruled out on the four idle windows (E100310, E100307, E100318 and E100321) and the E100318 swing plateaus. The tests are the phase errors under §1's phase method and the folded 36f and 42f amplitudes, read through the lifted joint fit and acquisition sampler in measurement.py and supply.py. A candidate that closes the 18f–30f phase errors within 30° is refitted on E100310 alone and re-scored on the held-out windows. Its result is recorded as a new model, not as an amendment of the frozen one. Negative control: a pure acquisition delay, whose phase error grows linearly with line order, is ruled out by the recorded pattern, where 6f and 12f are near zero and 18f–30f are not.

§14 — A coil-terminal resonance between 12f and 18f

§13 ruled out commutation overlap, the analogue bandwidth, which bridge leads and the base contribution. The recorded pattern is a step of nearly 180° between 12f, within 1°, and 18f–30f, at −143° to −160°. A second-order resonance between the two lines produces that step; a one-pole lag cannot. The candidate is an LC resonance in the coil loop between 12f and 18f, about 730–1100 Hz, and something must supply the C or the L. Against the 3.25 mH booster series inductance alone, the resonance needs 6.4–14.6 µF at the coil terminals or the converter output: 11–24× the documented 0.6 µF screen, which resonates with 3.25 mH near 3.6 kHz. With that 0.6 µF, the loop would instead need about 50 mH of series inductance. The CEA base's per-bridge DC reactors, in series with the coil in 2021, are one documented place it could come from (Plant Integration Document pp. 139–141, in data/sources/). Above the resonance, a two-pole response falls as 1/f². That would also attenuate the folded 36f (about 2.2 kHz) and 42f (about 2.6 kHz) lines, which the frozen model overpredicts about 10× and 2.3×. The same mechanism would also fit the training misses on E100310 at the two lines the fit did not match (it matched 6f, 18f and 30f by construction). 12f, below the proposed resonance, measures 238 V against 157 V modelled, where a resonance boost applies. 24f, above it, measures 44 V against 163 V, where the response falls.

Done when scripts/figures/booster_phase_diagnosis.py fits one resonance on E100310's line amplitudes and phases alone, with a damping resistance only if the data need it. It fits it two ways: as a shunt capacitance against the 3.25 mH series inductance, and as a series inductance against the documented 0.6 µF screen. Both are re-scored on the four 2021 idle windows and the E100318 plateaus under filter-grounding-prediction §1's phase method, with the folded 36f and 42f amplitudes in the bcm-overlay windows as a second check. A form is confirmed only if 6f, 12f and 18f–30f all fall within 30° on all four idle windows and the folded 36f and 42f amplitudes move toward the recorded ones. The fragment names the component that would supply the fitted C or L. It sets the value against the CEA base's DC reactor inductance, the 0.6 µF screen, and every terminal or snubber capacitance in the jt60sa-power-supply-sources registers and data/sources/, or records that none matches. The result is recorded as a candidate model, and fitted_parameters.py stays unchanged. The §13 review's two test-pin follow-ons are closed: the tests assert the diagnosis script's computed outputs rather than hard-coded numbers, and the delay rule-out is tested on both branches. No 2023 shot is read. Negative control: a capacitance that puts the resonance above 30f, at 2 kHz or more, leaves the step unexplained.

§15 — Does the base supply alone depend on the coil-current sign?

Filter-grounding-prediction §5 found that the measured 12f line falls about tenfold when the coil current reverses from about −2.8 kA to about +2.8 kA. The 2021 values are 386, 363 and 632 V against 41, 71 and 85 V on E100317 EF5, E100318 EF5 and E100324 EF2, and all four judged 2023 shots show the same pattern. 24f does not fall. The paired base of §8 and §10 gives nearly the same 12f for both signs, because each direction's module pair is a 30° pair. This section asks whether the base alone carries that sign dependence. §16 asks whether the booster does. A four-module, twenty-four-pulse base under positive current would cancel 12f and keep 24f. But §8's twelve EF3/EF4 windows (E100340 and E100342 EF4; E100344 and E100345 EF3) carry 1.1–5.0 kA, and their 12f lines (91–133 V) fit one 30° pair at 1.0 dB RMS. The fragments record the current magnitude only, not its sign. On those booster-free coils 12f stays near 100 V at a few kA, while on the booster coils EF2 and EF5 it falls tenfold under positive current. That points at the booster. This section establishes the sign of each window and settles whether the base contributes at all.

Done when the held 2021 shots (data/jt60sa/inventory.json) are searched for base-only windows of both current signs. The base-only windows are multi-kA windows on the booster-free coils EF3 and EF4, and windows on EF2 and EF5 where the booster reference and booster current are near zero. Each is scored at 12f and 24f with its current sign stated, and the §8 windows (fragments bcm-base-modules.html and bcm-base-pairs.html) are among them. If base-only windows of only one sign exist, the fragment records that and says what that sign alone settles. Each sign is scored with one 30° pair and with all four modules. The scoring calls the existing path and copies none of it. The model is supply.SupplyModel with the paired base, whose source-to-coil path is coil_phasors and acquired_phasors. The lines come from measurement.measure, and the windows are read through scripts/figures/base_supply_residuals.py, whose window reader and line helpers are extended rather than duplicated. The fragment records which mode each sign's 12f and 24f select, and reconciles that with §8's refutation through the signs of its windows. If a sign-dependent mode reproduces both signs within filter-grounding-prediction §1's bands, its base line voltage and reactance are refitted on 2021 and re-scored on held-out 2021 windows. That result is recorded as a candidate model, and src/power_convertor/fitted_parameters.py stays unchanged. No 2023 shot is read. If the base-only 12f shows no sign dependence beyond §1's bands, the base candidate is ruled out and the dependence is left to §16. Negative control: forcing the four-module base on §8's EF3/EF4 windows must fail their 12f lines. This section reads §8's landed window fragments as data, and does not need §8 to close.

§16 — Does the booster's other series pair conduct the other current sign?

Each booster is four converters in two series pairs connected antiparallel, so each pair conducts one current sign. The documented secondaries differ: PSV21–PSV22 at 2.9/2.9 kV and PSV11–PSV12 at 3.16/2.1 kV (jt60sa-power-supply-sources §2). The coil-to-winding crosswalk is open, so which pair carries which sign is not documented. The frozen model, fitted on E100310 EF5, uses PSV21/22 for both signs. Filter-grounding-prediction §5 found that the 2021 booster coils carry a 12f line roughly ten times stronger under negative coil current than under positive: 386 and 363 V against 41 and 71 V on E100317 and E100318 EF5, and 632 against 85 V on E100324 EF2. A pair with unequal secondaries changes the booster's whole line set, so it is a candidate for the booster-coil share of that dependence. On the booster-free coils EF3 and EF4, 12f stays near 100 V at 1.1–5.0 kA (§8, current sign not recorded), so the collapse appears only where a booster is present. If the conducting pair changes with the current sign, the booster's 12f may add to the base's 12f in phase under one sign and in antiphase under the other. §15 settles whether the base alone carries any sign dependence.

Done when every 2021 window of both current signs on EF2 and EF5 is scored at 6f, 12f, 18f, 24f and 30f, with each window's current sign stated and the frozen base held fixed. Two pair assignments are scored for each sign: PSV21/22 (the frozen fit) and PSV11/12 at 3.16/2.1 kV. The scoring calls scripts/figures/booster_firing_law.py's model_for and predicted, with the pair's secondaries set through SupplyModel.booster_line_voltage and booster_second_line_voltage. The lines come from measurement.measure and copy no fitting logic. For each sign, the booster's 12f phasor is reported beside the base's, with the phase between them. The fragment records which pair each sign selects, and whether E100310's current sign agrees with PSV21/22 having been fitted there. If a sign-dependent assignment reproduces both signs within filter-grounding-prediction §1's bands, it is recorded as a candidate model with its PSV11/12 reactance refitted on 2021 alone. src/power_convertor/fitted_parameters.py stays unchanged, and no 2023 shot is read. Negative control: assigning PSV11/12 to E100310's own current sign must worsen that window's lines against the frozen fit.

§17 — Why the model's booster and base 12f interfere the wrong way round

§16 scored eighteen 2021 booster-coil windows and recorded the booster's 12f phasor beside the base's. In the model, the two lie about 156° apart under negative current, so they partly cancel to about 157 V. Under positive current they lie −3° to +56° apart and add to 380–415 V. The measured lines do the opposite. Under negative current 12f is 220–370 V, larger than the model, and under positive current it is 41–85 V, far smaller. Measured, the booster and base 12f add under negative current and cancel under positive. The model has that interference reversed.

The documents fix three structural facts the model departs from (Plant Integration Document v2.9 p. 140, Fig. 2.7-4, rendered at data/sources/base-plant-page-001.png, and the MECS limit table data/sources/B-6_ps_limit_table.datの設定v2.pdf).

  • The booster transformers' phases. On EF2 and EF5 the booster transformers are labelled −7.5° and +22.5°, against the base's 0, −30, +15 and −15°. The model takes the booster pair as 0° and 30°, relative displacement only (configurations.py). Under the shared exp(i·n·φ) convention of BridgePair and BridgeSet, the documented labels turn booster line n by −n·7.5°, which is −90° at 12f. That holds only if the booster and base transformers share one 18 kV bus and one label convention. The table gives 18 kV for both, but a common bus is not confirmed.
  • Which base modules conduct which sign. The 0° and −30° modules ("836V/±5kA ×2units") are bidirectional. The +15° and −15° modules ("836V/−5kA ×2units") conduct negative current only. Positive current can therefore flow only through the 0/−30 pair, which is the model's assignment, so a module swap contradicts the drawing. Under negative current all four modules can conduct: a twenty-four-pulse set that cancels the base's 12f, which the model does not allow. The ENEA analogue is EF1/EF6 state 5, parallel operation in reverse. The limits, +10 kA and −20 kA on EF2 and EF5, match two modules forward and four in reverse, and indicate a straight current-reversing link rather than a crossed one.
  • 12f alone cannot separate the arms. Any uniform 15° booster-to-base shift flips the 12f interference exactly as a module swap does, so only 6f, 18f, 24f and 30f can tell the arms apart.

Done when every 2021 EF2 and EF5 window of both current signs scored in §16 is re-scored under four arms, with the frozen booster and base voltages and reactances held fixed. The arms are scored in this order:

  1. The documented booster phases, −7.5° and +22.5° against the base.
  2. The four-module base under negative current.
  3. Both of those together.
  4. The module swap (+15/−15 under positive current), scored and reported only, because the drawing contradicts it.

Every line from 6f to 30f is scored in amplitude and phase, after one fitted supply phase per window. The scoring runs through the script §16's node built: scripts/figures/booster_pair_sign.py, which calls scripts/figures/booster_firing_law.py's model_for and predicted, with measurement.measure. Its window loader and band check are replaced by prediction.py's, which they duplicate. The arm changes are made through the configuration and the existing BridgePair and BridgeSet phases, not by rotating output phasors. The fragment reports, for each sign and arm, the booster-to-base 12f phase and every line's amplitude and phase error. Its verdict rests on 6f, 18f, 24f and 30f as well as 12f. An arm that brings every line of both signs within filter-grounding-prediction §1's bands is refitted on 2021 alone and re-scored on the held-out 2021 windows. That result is recorded as a candidate model, and src/power_convertor/fitted_parameters.py stays unchanged. The §8 EF3/EF4 windows are re-scored under arms 2 and 3. On EF3 and EF4 all four modules are bidirectional: "836V/±5kA×4units" on PID p. 141, Fig. 2.7-5, rendered at data/sources/base-plant-page-002.png, with a ±20 kA limit. So those windows (1.1–5.0 kA, of whatever sign) allowed four-module conduction and showed one 30° pair: four modules predict no 12f against 91–133 V measured. That is the CEA base running as one pair at a few kA when four could conduct. It bears on arm 2 by analogy, not proof, since the two converters may be controlled differently. Arm 2 is supported only if the EF2/EF5 negative-current windows show the 12f cancellation that EF3/EF4 did not, and the fragment states the comparison. A negative-current EF3/EF4 window, if §15 finds one, is the cleanest booster-free test of arm 2. No 2023 shot is read. Negative control: the booster shift at the documented magnitude but the wrong sign (+7.5°, +90° at 12f) is scored beside arm 1. A verdict that cannot tell −7.5° from +7.5° on 6f–30f confirms nothing. If the wrong sign scores better than the documented one on any line, the documented phases are recorded as not supported on that line.

For each sign, the fragment also reports the single booster-to-base 12f rotation that best fits all windows of that sign, and the spread it leaves between windows. A bound computed from §16's phases, not from a run: arm 1 can move positive-current 12f by only about −3 to +1 dB, against the 13–20 dB the measurement needs. A tenfold drop needs the booster and base 12f within about ±11–23° of antiphase, and the model's positive windows spread across 59°. If no uniform rotation closes the positive side, the fragment says so, and names the part of the model that would have to vary between windows, such as the booster's firing angle with its operating point.

§18 — What the base supply does at zero voltage reference

In booster-idle windows, the base's 12f line tracks the base voltage reference, not the coil-current sign (§15). Near zero reference it is about 10–20 V; at 200–330 V it is about 100 V. The paired base predicts about 100 V at either reference. In 2021, E100317 and E100318 EF5 at zero reference and +2.8 kA measure 15.7 V and 11.1 V of 12f, against 106.2 V and 102.6 V predicted. That is the reverse of a phase-controlled bridge. With no overlap, a six-pulse bridge's line n scales as √(cos²α + n² sin²α)/(n²−1), so zero output, with firing near 90°, gives about twelve times the 12f of full output. A JAEA design study (Shimada et al., data/sources/base-stable-current.pdf) describes three unit states: positive, negative, and suspended (gate block). The units combine into parallel, single-converter and circulating operation, with design thresholds of −5, −1, +2 and +6 kA rising and −6, −2, +1 and +5 kA falling. At 2.8 kA those thresholds give single-converter operation. They are design values, not the installed CEA thresholds. Circulating operation applies below 1 kA (Novello 2015). No bypass or freewheel mode appears in the documents held under data/sources/, where every "BPS" is the switching-network or quench-protection bypass switch. Those documents do not include CEA's EF2–EF5 operating-mode description: the ENEA procurement specification (§4.4.3.12–13) leaves those modes to CEA. Their absence therefore marks a gap in the record, not evidence against such a mode.

Each candidate leaves a distinct line signature:

  • one 30° pair, phase-controlled near 90°: 12f and 24f both present;
  • all four modules in one direction: 12f cancelled, 24f kept;
  • signed circulating operation at 90°: 12f kept, 24f cancelled;
  • blocked or bypassed: both absent from the base's own output.

Done when every 2021 base-only window from §15 is scored with its base reference stated, on the traces already held in data/jt60sa/. The EF3/EF4 shots of §8 are not held as traces; their fetch and re-score are §19. A base-only window has both booster references idle and a coil current of at least 1 kA; a zero-reference window has a base reference within 20 V of zero. Each window is scored at 12f and 24f on two channels: the coil voltage MMSYS/vol<coil>, and the base's own DC voltage <coil>/volPSDC at 4 kHz. The coil voltage is measured with measurement.measure. Where <coil>/volPSDC is tapped, and its bandwidth and calibration, are not documented (jt60sa-power-supply-sources §7). In §15's booster-idle windows its mean agrees with the coil voltage's within 40 V, which places it on the base's DC side, so the 12f and 24f it carries are reported as measured on that channel, with that limit stated, and not asserted to be the ripple at the base's output terminals. The base DC voltage is read by extending read_window in scripts/figures/base_supply_residuals.py to return the <coil>/volPSDC trace over the same window, and its lines are measured with measurement.measure_window, the same line fit measure applies to the coil voltage. The fragment tabulates, per window, the measured 12f and 24f on both channels beside each candidate signature. It records which signature the zero-reference windows match, and whether the base's DC voltage carries the ripple the coil does not. On EF2 and EF5 a four-module signature under positive current would conflict with the −5 kA rating of the +15/−15 modules, and the fragment says so if one appears. A candidate that matches is written into the base model as a reference-dependent mode, refitted on 2021 alone, and recorded as a candidate model. src/power_convertor/fitted_parameters.py stays unchanged. No 2023 shot is read. On the coil channel, the zero-reference 12f recorded in §15 is 11–16 V, between the listed signatures' predictions of about 100 V and about 0 V; the base DC channel may differ, which is what it is scored to show. If no signature passes on a channel, the fragment states the amplitude and phase the data require there and which signature comes closest, and records no candidate model. Negative control: the frozen paired base, which predicts about 100 V of 12f at both references, must fail the zero-reference windows' 12f while passing at least one of §15's 252–328 V windows, so the scoring is shown to discriminate between the two reference levels. Beside it, the fragment reports the textbook phase-control scaling, a six-pulse pair without overlap fired at the window's reference, as a comparison. It predicts more 12f at zero reference than at 200–330 V, the opposite of the measured trend. A test runs base_only_main, the script's entry point, over an inventory holding a 2023 shot and a window whose booster carries voltage, and shows neither reaches the scored set, so the 2023 filter and the booster-voltage check are pinned at the entry point as well as in collect_base_only_windows.

Amended 2026-10-14: the three zero-reference windows run at a 60.70–60.75 Hz fundamental, where measure_window could not lock 12f before §20. The 11–16 V premise above and the negative control built on it therefore rest on a misread line. bcm-zero-reference delivered this section's scoring machinery on that reading. No further node is dispatched on this section. It closes on §21, which re-judges these windows and this negative control on the corrected readings.

§20 — The 12f line locked at the supply's own frequency

measure_window in src/power_convertor/measurement.py seeds its 6f and 12f anchors at a fixed 61.2 Hz fundamental, and fold.fit_line searches ±3 Hz around each seed. The 12f anchor can therefore lock only at a fundamental of 60.95–61.45 Hz, and the 6f anchor only at 60.70–61.70 Hz. Late in a shot the motor-generator runs at 60.65–60.87 Hz. There the 12f anchor lands on the edge of its search band and reads the skirt of the line. Every line seeded from a mis-locked anchor inherits the error, and so do the reported supply frequency and the 12f family fold. A per-order frequency scan of the held traces reads coil 12f of 91.5–110.8 V at 60.70–60.75 Hz in the zero-reference windows of E100317, E100318 and E100324, where measure_window reads 10.8–15.7 V. Windows at 61.0–61.2 Hz, E100310 among them, are unaffected.

Done when measure_window locks both anchors at the window's own fundamental anywhere in 60.0–61.6 Hz, and refuses a window whose 6f and 12f anchors disagree at the fundamental by more than a stated tolerance. A synthetic window at 60.70 Hz carrying known 6f–30f lines is measured within 0.1 dB in amplitude and 0.01 Hz in frequency on every line, and its 12f family fold matches the synthetic waveform. The same test fails under the fixed 61.2 Hz seeding (negative control). The existing tests in tests/test_measurement.py pass unchanged, and a log on the held traces shows E100310's lines moving by less than 0.1 dB. The fragment records, for the zero-reference windows of E100317, E100318 and E100324, the fundamental each anchor locks at and the coil 12f, before and after the change. The manifest lists the other fixed 61.2 Hz seeds, such as scripts/jt60sa/inventory.py, without changing them. No landed window is re-scored here; that is §21.

§21 — Re-score the windows the 12f lock misread

§20 changes the 12f reading on every window whose fundamental is below about 60.95 Hz, and every quantity seeded from it. Three landed conclusions rest on those readings:

  • §15's finding that 12f follows the base voltage reference, at 13 V at zero reference;
  • §17's numbers for the positive-current booster windows;
  • §18's findings that no candidate signature fits the zero-reference windows and that <coil>/volPSDC sits at its fit floor.

§5's judged held-out cases include late-shot windows of E100307 and E100318.

The phases rest on the same misread fundamental as the amplitudes. prediction.py takes the measured f_supply for three things: the model's synthesis frequency, the four-cycle joint line coefficients and the fitted supply phase. scripts/figures/base_supply_residuals.py takes each row's frequency, and both channels' phasors, from it. The landed fundamentals of the late windows sit 0.12–0.37 Hz above the true ones. Over one four-cycle window that walks the 24f phasor by about 69–210°. The hard-coded rows in LANDED_BASE_ONLY_WINDOWS carry each window's landed frequency and 12f, and the drift tests pin them to the landed records. If a row and its record are both wrong, the tests stay green.

Done when every window behind those conclusions, and every one of §5's judged held-out cases, is re-scored through measure_window as §20 leaves it. The frozen parameters in src/power_convertor/fitted_parameters.py stay unchanged and nothing is refitted. The fragment tabulates, for each window:

  • the fitted fundamental;
  • the old and new 12f;
  • the old and new phase of every judged line;
  • the base DC 12f where it is held;
  • the verdict under the bands of filter-grounding-prediction §1, beside the landed value.

A window that §20's measurement refuses is tabulated as refused, with both anchors' frequencies, and counts as unscored in every verdict. Phase verdicts are re-judged alongside amplitudes. Each re-scored base-only row is computed from its held trace through measure_window, and no row is copied from a record. Where a hard-coded row is kept, it changes in the same commit as the record it is pinned to. The record states that its values were re-scored, beside the values it first landed. The residual-against-frequency-sag comparison in that script is re-run on the corrected fundamentals. The fragment names each landed conclusion that changes, with its old and new figures, and states §5's aggregate verdict on the re-scored cases. This shows the re-score changes only the windows the old lock misread. No 2023 shot is read; the 2023 swing windows are re-judged in filter-grounding-prediction.

§22 — The booster branch that carries positive current

No frozen parameter was identified at positive current. PSV21/22's commutation reactance was fitted on E100310 at −3304 A. Two sources rate the booster's positive branch far below its negative one:

  • the EF1 drawing labels “Booster PS ±5kV/+4kA (full load)” and “Booster PS ±5kV/−14.5kA (full load)” (Coletti 2011, p. 1374, Fig. 4; jt60sa-booster-ripple-evidence papers-system-and-base);
  • the MECS limit logic gives the booster's rated current as −14.5 kA to +4 kA, applied as −14.3/+3.8 kA since MECS v2.8.1 of 2020-12-17 (MECSfeat_eng and MECSver_eng pages, held in the imas-codex graph).

The four positive windows carry 2304 A (E100318 EF5), 2322 A (E100324 EF2), 2982 A (E100317 EF5) and 3989 A (E100319 EF2) (bcm-interference). They load that branch to 58–100% of its rating, against 16–28% of the −14.5 kA branch. Commutation overlap grows with per-unit current times per-unit reactance and cuts the higher lines steeply. The re-scored positive windows (§21) fit that shape: 6f passes on 4 of 4, 12f measures 112–251 V against 380–415 V modelled, and 18f is 10–20 dB over. §16's pair swap kept the frozen reactance, so it did not test a smaller branch.

Done when the positive branch's commutation reactance is fitted on one pre-registered positive window, E100318 EF5 6.5–7.5 s. At most its secondary voltage is fitted alongside it, held within 10% of a documented pair. Without refitting, the result predicts the other three positive windows: E100317 EF5 7.5–8.5 s, E100324 EF2 6.5–7.5 s and E100319 EF2 −3.5 to −1.0 s. The fragment:

  • judges 6f, 12f and 18f amplitude against filter-grounding-prediction §1's bands;
  • reports 24f, 30f and every phase, naming the shared 18f–30f phase step of §13 and §14;
  • reports the fitted reactance as a transformer %Z at the +4 kA rating;
  • tabulates a leave-one-out fit over the four windows;
  • reports E100317's verdict with its operation-log flag beside it (“波形がおかしいので、電源Grにて調査”). E100318 is the logged repeat.

The fourteen negative windows keep PSV21/22 and move by less than 0.1 dB. Negative control: the fitted positive-branch reactance, applied to the negative windows, worsens them. The result is a candidate model only: src/power_convertor/fitted_parameters.py is unchanged and no 2023 shot is read.

§23 — The model along whole 2021 pulses

Every verdict so far rests on a few chosen windows. This section steps a 1.0 s window by 0.1 s through each held 2021 EF2 and EF5 shot. EF3 and EF4 follow once §19 lands.

For each window it:

  • measures the 6f–30f amplitudes and phases with measure_window, and the family-folded peak-to-peak;
  • records the base reference, booster voltage reference, booster current reference, the coil-current mean and sign, the locked fundamental, and whether the booster carries voltage (the coil-mean against <coil>/volPSDC test);
  • predicts the window through prediction.py at its own operating point: firing from the reference, overlap from the current's magnitude, and one fitted supply phase per window. The frozen model uses PSV21/22 for both current signs, because which pair carries which sign is not documented (§16). The sign therefore enters only as a regime label, not as a choice of pair.

A 1.0 s window keeps §20's anchor-agreement refusal at its full 0.1 Hz.

Done when each shot has one figure: references and current, measured against modelled 6f, 12f and 18f, and peak-to-peak. One table gives the pass fraction for each line in each regime: base-only, booster negative, booster positive, and transition. Transition windows are those where the sign, the booster state or a reference steps inside the window; they are scored apart, because a quasi-static model is not expected to hold there. A refused window is tabulated as refused.

The frozen parameters are used and no 2023 shot is read. Negative control: each window given the operating point of a window of the other sign or reference loses pass fraction, which shows the comparison resolves operating-point dependence. The section reuses measure_window, prediction.py's loader and band check, booster_pair_sign.py's arms and base_supply_residuals.read_window for volPSDC, with no new loader. Once §22 lands, its candidate is a second model curve on the same figures.

§24 — Which base pair conducts at positive current

§8 carries the base's one-direction mode as the 30°-apart module pair for the current's direction: 0°/−30° at positive current and +15°/−15° at negative. The assignment is inferred, not cited. At positive coil current, 12f runs +1.98 to +10.61 dB high and 24f +6.23 to +15.61 dB high on every booster window, and §22 rules out the branch reactance. The two assignments differ by 15° in the pair's mean phase, which is 180° at 12f and 360° at 24f. Swapping the positive-current pair therefore reverses the base's 12f against the booster's and leaves 24f unchanged. It can account for the 12f excess, not the 24f.

Score the positive-current booster windows of §17 and §22 under both assignments, holding the documented booster phases and every other frozen value. Done when a fragment tabulates, per window, 12f and 24f amplitude and phase under each assignment beside the measurement; states whether the swap brings 12f inside its §1 band of filter-grounding-prediction and whether 24f stays unchanged, as predicted; and shows 12f measured against both assignments in one figure. Negative control: the fourteen negative-current windows, which keep the +15°/−15° pair in both arms, move by less than 0.01 dB. The frozen parameters are unchanged and no 2023 shot is read. The section reuses booster_pair_sign.py's window reader and arms without editing that file.

§ Decisions

Is the model judged on harmonic lines or on time-domain waveforms?

Harmonic lines are robust to the arbitrary supply phase at the start of a window and to noise, and they are what a filter acts on. Time-domain folded waveforms also carry phase between harmonics, which a twelve-pulse pair changes, but they need the alignment step and are sensitive to the digitiser images.

The lead chose to judge each line's phase as well as its amplitude, alongside the folded peak-to-peak, which this decision already judged under the earlier choice 'both' (lines and fold). The reason is a measurement. Once the frozen 2021 model is shifted by one supply phase onto the recorded samples, it reproduces the idle 6f waveform. Its 18f, 24f and 30f phases sit more than 100° from the measured ones on every idle window, including its training window E100310, while the amplitude bands pass at 6f and 18f. An amplitude score cannot see that error in the waveform's shape. One common shift is the only freedom allowed, because no recorded channel gives the supply phase; a phase per line would let any model with the right amplitudes match. The coordinator proposed the 30° band: a 30° error moves a line's vector by about half its amplitude, the same order as a 3 dB amplitude miss (0.41). Lines below 10 V are reported, not judged. The criterion is registered in filter-grounding-prediction §1, before any 2023 prediction was computed. The peak-to-peak ripple stays judged because it is the quantity the model exists to reproduce: quench detection and the terminal insulation's Paschen margin see it. The harmonic lines are how the model is diagnosed and how the filter acts. All three are judged under the bands pre-registered in filter-grounding-prediction §1.

§2, §3 and §4 can run in parallel: the bridge library, the measurement chain and the circuit identification touch different modules. §5 waits on all three and on the acceptance criteria pre-registered in filter-grounding-prediction §1.

The coil-voltage channels carry a DC shift once their supply energises. On the 2023 kind-E shots E101001 and E101005, every MMSYS/vol<coil> moves by up to 28 V between supplies off and supplies on: CS1 −22.3 to −42.4 V, EF5 +33.4 to +40.4 V. This is recorded in jt60sa-coil-circuit-model §7. The base-only selection here compares the window-mean coil voltage with <coil>/volPSDC under a 40 V tolerance. The kept windows depart by 19.7–31.5 V, the size of that shift, so most of the tolerance may be spent on it. Whether the 2021 channels carry the same shift, and whether it is instrumentation or a current-dependent voltage, is not established. Harmonic lines are unaffected.

The shift is not uniform across coils. On the 2023 kind-E shots it runs −18 to −28 V on CS and −1.6 to +11 V on EF. For EF2 and EF5, then, it explains at most about a third of the 19.7–31.5 V departures the base-only windows keep. No held 2021 trace has a supplies-off window: E100310 opens mid-ramp. Settling it for 2021 needs one base-only shot re-fetched from about −45 s through scripts/jt60sa/fetch_traces.py. Then compare the channel's mean in three windows: supplies off, energised at the window's coil current, and after the pulse. The energised offset mode of slow_currents.py computes those levels. Separating instrumentation offset from a current-dependent voltage needs energised flats at two currents.

Coordinator decision on the bcm-measure node's halt: the acquisition model gains an interleave timing skew beside the gain mismatch and the bandwidth. In E100310 the image-to-line ratios grow with frequency: 0.121, 0.236, 0.383 and 0.524 at 6f, 12f, 18f and 24f. A gain mismatch gives one constant ratio, and the best gain-only chain misses by 62.4%. The skew is about 42% of the 250 µs sample period, large enough to be recorded as an open question about the digitiser.
